title: Periodic Functions and Why sin(x squared) Is Not One
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Define a periodic function, state the period of sin x, and argue carefully that the oscillating-looking function sin(x^2) is not periodic.
finalAnswer: $f$ is periodic when $f(x+T) = f(x)$ for all $x$ and some fixed $T > 0$; $\sin x$ has period $2\pi$, but $\sin(x^2)$ is not periodic because its zero crossings $x = \sqrt{n\pi}$ get progressively closer together.

steps.title: State the Definition Precisely
steps.mathExpression: \exists T > 0 \ \text{such that} \ f(x+T) = f(x) \ \text{for every } x \in D
steps.explanation: Periodicity demands a single fixed shift T that reproduces the entire graph, and the identity must hold for every input in the domain, whose shape must itself repeat (for all reals, typically). The smallest such T, when it exists, is called the period.
steps.why: The words for all x and fixed T are exactly what later arguments test or violate.

steps.title: Confirm a Standard Example
steps.explanation: The sine function repeats every full turn of the unit circle, so 2*pi is a period; no smaller positive shift works because sine takes each value exactly twice per cycle in a pattern that cannot repeat sooner. Cosine shares the period 2*pi; tangent repeats every pi.
steps.why: Grounding the definition in the cleanest example sets the comparison point for the counterexample.

steps.title: Diagnose sin(x squared)
steps.explanation: Suppose a period T existed. Zeros of a periodic function repeat with spacing T forever, but the zeros of sin(x^2) sit at sqrt(n*pi), whose consecutive gaps shrink toward 0 as n grows. The oscillations speed up: the wave never copies a previous window exactly, so no single T can satisfy the identity for all x.
steps.why: A gap sequence between zeros that is not constant directly contradicts the requirement of an exact repeating pattern.

steps.title: Heed the Graphical Lesson
steps.explanation: A quick graph of sin(x^2) shows waves pressed ever more tightly as |x| increases. Pictures can mislead about periodicity, so pair visual inspection with an argument about the spacing of zeros or peaks.
steps.why: Learning when a visual pattern fails to be periodic is a core review-skill takeaway.
